title: Transitions and timing functions
learningObjectives: Explain transitions and timing functions and apply it in an accessible responsive interface.

understand.concept: CSS transitions animate changes between property values over time. transition-property selects the properties, transition-duration sets time, transition-timing-function controls the rate curve, and transition-delay postpones the start. Prefer transitioning specific properties rather than using all without reason.
understand.whyItMatters: Transitions can make state changes easier to follow, but excessive or slow movement can delay interaction. Respect prefers-reduced-motion and avoid animating layout-heavy properties when a transform or opacity can achieve the effect.
understand.analogy: A transition is like a dimmer switch changing light smoothly rather than jumping instantly.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; transforms and animations follow the CSS rendering and timing model.

explain.narrative: The button changes background and position over a short transition; reduced-motion users receive the state change without movement.

examples.explanation: The button changes background and position over a short transition; reduced-motion users receive the state change without movement.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the relevant responsive or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Add transitions for a card's background and transform. Include a reduced-motion override and test keyboard focus.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that demonstrates the concept. Check keyboard access and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Test more than one viewport size.
Keep essential information available without motion.
Use developer tools to inspect computed values.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Transitions and timing functions</title></head><body>
<button class='button'>Hover or focus</button><style>.button{padding:.8rem 1rem;background:#dceaf2;border:1px solid #456;transition:background-color .2s ease,transform .2s ease}.button:hover,.button:focus-visible{background:#cde7dc;transform:translateY(-2px)}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.button{transition:none}.button:hover,.button:focus-visible{transform:none}}</style>
</body></html>
practice.resetCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Transitions and timing functions</title></head><body>
<button class='button'>Hover or focus</button><style>.button{padding:.8rem 1rem;background:#dceaf2;border:1px solid #456;transition:background-color .2s ease,transform .2s ease}.button:hover,.button:focus-visible{background:#cde7dc;transform:translateY(-2px)}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.button{transition:none}.button:hover,.button:focus-visible{transform:none}}</style>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which transition property controls the rate curve of an animation?
questions.explanation: transition-timing-function defines how intermediate values are calculated over time.

questions.prompt: What should be done for users who prefer reduced motion?
questions.explanation: Respect the user's preference while preserving content and interaction.
